standard_prerequisites.name: K-injective resolutions and the computation of right derived functors on acyclics
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Injectives, the theorem providing a K-injective embedding, the lemma that direct sums of K-injectives represent direct sums, and Derived Categories, the lemma computing an unbounded right derived functor on a complex of acyclics
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the representatives used to compute R Gamma(U, direct sum of K_i).

core_obligations: Reduce to the derived global sections (proof lines 14148-14153): since Hom(j_!O_U, K) = R Gamma(U, K), it suffices to show that R Gamma(U, -) commutes with direct sums, and assumptions (1) and (2) mean that F = H^0(U, -) has finite cohomological dimension and that direct sums of injectives are acyclic for F.
Choose K-injective representatives (proof lines 14154-14159): take K-injective complexes I_i^bullet with injective terms representing the objects K_i, using the K-injective embedding theorem.

Conclude the commutation (proof lines 14160-14164): the right derived functor of F may be computed on any complex of acyclics and the direct sum of the K_i is represented by the direct sum of the I_i^bullet, so R Gamma(U, direct sum K_i) is represented by the direct sum of the complexes H^0(U, I_i^bullet); hence R Gamma(U, -) commutes with direct sums and j_!O_U is compact.
proof_roadmap: Replace the compactness statement by commutation of the derived global sections with direct sums.
Choose K-injective representatives of the summands so that the direct sum represents the direct sum in the derived category.
Compute the right derived functor on this complex of acyclics to obtain the commutation.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives conditions under which j_!O_U is compact in the derived category: bounded cohomological dimension on U together with commutation of the cohomology functors with direct sums (statement lines 14135-14145). The proof (proof lines 14147-14164) reduces compactness to commutation of R Gamma(U, -) with direct sums, chooses K-injective representatives of the summands, and computes the derived functor on that complex of acyclics. H2: one reduction and one resolution argument, written out.
